name: Portsea Surf Beach

facts.claim: Portsea Surf Beach is an ocean beach within Mornington Peninsula National Park, on the Bass Strait side of Portsea.
Portsea, Sorrento and Gunnamatta surf beaches are patrolled during summer holidays.
Parks Victoria lists it among the national park's surf beaches for surfing, swimming and rockpool exploring.

name: Gunnamatta Beach

facts.claim: Gunnamatta Beach is a surf beach in Mornington Peninsula National Park, noted by Parks Victoria as a draw for experienced surfers.
Gunnamatta is one of the park's ocean beaches along with Flinders, Portsea and Rye.
Patrolled during summer holidays.

name: Coolart Wetlands and Homestead

facts.claim: Coolart is a wetlands reserve and historic homestead at 40 Lord Somers Rd, Somers, on Western Port Bay.
The wetlands are open daily; the homestead and shop open Wednesday, Saturday and Sunday only.
Dogs are not permitted, under Parks Victoria regulations.
The site has a community garden and rose garden around the homestead.

name: Mornington

facts.claim: Mornington is the largest town on the peninsula's Port Phillip side, with a main street running down to the pier and foreshore.
Its Mornington Racecourse is in the town.
It is the main shopping and cafe centre of the eastern peninsula.

name: McCrae Homestead

facts.claim: McCrae Homestead was home to artist Georgiana McCrae, who arrived in 1845 and drew the plan for the house herself.
It gives a view of domestic life in the 1840s.
The Burrell Gallery in the homestead tells a family's story on the Mornington Peninsula over 75 years.
It is run by the National Trust and sits at 11 Beverley Road, McCrae.

name: The Briars

facts.claim: The Briars is one of the oldest homesteads on the Mornington Peninsula, surrounded by a wildlife sanctuary and vineyards.
Napoleon memorabilia collected by Dame Mabel Brookes, including Bonaparte's writing table, is displayed in the homestead.
The precinct has a visitor centre, wetlands, gardens, cafe and picnic areas with free BBQs.
Entry to the park is free.
